Dr. Travis Wrenn
Punt Road Medical Clinic
172 Punt Road
Mosman. 2088.

17 January 2016

Re: Miss Cassandra Kinser, aged 32 years

Dear Dr Wrenn,

A patient of yours, Miss Kinser, was admitted to St Vincent's Hospital
today due to a lip laceration and burning urination. This letter is to
refer her to you for further medical evaluation.

On admission today, Miss Kinser was treated for an infected lip
laceration, resulting from an alleged assault by her boyfriend for
which she had not sought medical care. Due to a burning sensation
when urinating for the past few days, she was diagnosed with a
urinary tract infection. We have also made an appointment for a
consultation at the sexual health clinic as Miss Kinser is sexually
active and does not use protection.

Today Miss Kinser’s lip infection was treated with Cipro, Clindamycin
and Oxycodone, all of which are to be continued until finished. She
has also been given Peridex mouthwash to be used regularly. The
dosage and frequency of these are included in side notes for your
reference. The patient is being discharged today in a stable
condition.

Would you kindly assess the patient regarding her lip laceration and
antibiotics course and her possible UTI. In addition, please follow up
on her sexual health clinic appointment for suspected STD.

Please contact me if you have further enquiries.

Yours sincerely,

Charge Nurse
